Use cluster analysis software to analyze the HEX and FAM fluorescent signal data. If using a CFX Opus 384 Real-Time PCR System and Bio-Rad CFX Maestro TM 2.3 software, use default settings on the “Allelic discrimination” table. The target is present in samples producing both HEX and FAM fluorescent signals ( Figure 2 ). The target is absent in samples producing only HEX signals. Ensure the negative and positive controls are present in the expected clusters. See Troubleshooting if markers do not perform as expected ( Figures 3 –6). steps.title: Design and order primers
steps.instruction: Design four primers: a forward and reverse target‑specific primer (TSP) and a forward and reverse core‑gene‑specific primer (CGSP). Follow the design guidelines (single‑copy gene, 5–100 bp amplicon, Tm 57–60 °C, length 18–30 bp, GC 40–60 %, no >3 consecutive G/C at 3′ end, avoid hairpins, dimers, repeats). Add the FAM tail (5′‑GAAGGTGACCAAGTTCATGCT‑3′) to the 5′ end of the forward TSP and the HEX tail (5′‑GAAGGTCGGAGTCAACGGATT‑3′) to the 5′ end of the forward CGSP. Order the primers from a DNA‑oligo supplier.

substeps.instruction: Design primers using a tool such as Primer3.
Check that at least one primer has high 3′‑end specificity (SNPs/indels).
Add fluorescent tails to forward primers.
Order primers.

steps.title: Prepare FAASA primer mix
steps.instruction: Combine the four primers at the concentrations shown in Recipe 1 to obtain a 73× primer mix (total 100 µL).

substeps.instruction: Add 12 µL of 100 µM FAM‑tagged forward TSP (12 µM final).
Add 30 µL of 100 µM reverse TSP (30 µM final).
Add 12 µL of 100 µM HEX‑tagged forward CGSP (12 µM final).
Add 30 µL of 100 µM reverse CGSP (30 µM final).
Add 16 µL ddH₂O to bring the volume to 100 µL.
Mix well, store at –20 °C, and bring to room temperature before use.

steps.title: Prepare FAASA master mix
steps.instruction: Make the master mix for the desired number of reactions using the FAASA primer mix, 2× PACE genotyping master mix, and ddH₂O as in Recipe 2 (4.055 µL per 384‑well reaction).

substeps.instruction: For each reaction add 0.055 µL FAASA primer mix (1×).
Add 2 µL 2× PACE genotyping master mix (1×).
Add 2 µL ddH₂O (1×).
Vortex to mix thoroughly.
Prepare enough mix for the total number of wells plus extra (e.g., 1 703.1 µL for 384 reactions).
Aliquot the mix into 8‑well strip tubes or a single column of a 96‑well plate (use the “volume per well in 8 wells” values).

steps.title: Dilute samples and load DNA
steps.instruction: Dilute each DNA sample to the appropriate concentration, add controls, and dispense 3 µL into each well of a 384‑well PCR plate.

substeps.instruction: Select a positive control (target present), a negative control (target absent but core gene present), and a non‑template control (NTC) containing only PCR‑grade ddH₂O.
Dilute samples to 25–35 ng/µL (if measuring ssDNA + dsDNA) or 12–17 ng/µL (if measuring dsDNA only).
Pipette 3 µL of each diluted sample (or control) into the bottom of a well of a 384‑well plate; avoid touching the well sides.
If desired, load each sample in duplicate on the plate.

steps.title: Dry and pre‑PCR plate preparation
steps.instruction: Seal, centrifuge, and dry the DNA‑loaded plate before adding master mix.

substeps.instruction: Cover the plate with a temporary adhesive sealing film (optical clarity not required).
Centrifuge at ≥300 × g for 10 s to collect DNA at the well bottom.
Place the sealed plate in an oven at 65 °C for 1–1.5 h to dry the samples.
Allow the plate to cool at room temperature for 15–20 min (or store dried plate at RT for later use).

steps.title: Add master mix and seal plate
steps.instruction: Dispense FAASA master mix onto the dried DNA, seal with an optically clear film, and mix.

substeps.instruction: Work under dim light; keep the 2× PACE master mix protected from light (thaw in a drawer or covered box, use small aliquots frozen at –20 °C).
Dispense 4 µL of FAASA master mix into each well of the 384‑well plate (the master mix can be added on top of the dried DNA without touching the well sides).
Seal the plate with a new optically clear adhesive sealing film using a film applicator; avoid touching the film with bare hands.
Centrifuge the sealed plate at ≥300 × g for 10 s.
Mix the plate on a plate mixer at 2 600 rpm for 45 s, then centrifuge again at ≥300 × g for 10 s.
Wipe the outer surface of the sealing film with 70 % (v/v) ethanol.

steps.title: Run PCR cycling and read fluorescence
steps.instruction: Program the thermocycler with the FAASA cycling profile, run the PCR, and acquire fluorescence data.

substeps.instruction: Initial denaturation/ enzyme activation: 94 °C for 15 min (1 cycle).
Denaturation: 94 °C for 20 s (10 cycles).
Annealing & extension (first phase): 65 °C for 1 min (10 cycles).
Denaturation: 94 °C for 20 s (30 cycles).
Annealing & extension (second phase): 57 °C for 1 min (30 cycles).
Optional pre‑read cool‑down (real‑time instrument only): 12 °C for 10 s.
Immediately read the plate on a real‑time PCR machine or a separate fluorescent plate reader (detect FAM, HEX, and ROX channels).
If clusters are not well separated, add extra cycles in 3‑cycle increments (Table 2):
– 3 cycles of 94 °C 20 s, 57 °C 1 min, then a 12 °C 30 s pre‑read; read fluorescence after each increment until tight, separated clusters are obtained (maximum recommended 9 extra cycles).

steps.title: Analyze fluorescence data
steps.instruction: Use cluster‑analysis software to interpret the FAM and HEX signals and call alleles.

substeps.instruction: Load the fluorescence data into the instrument’s analysis software (e.g., Bio‑Rad CFX Maestro 2.3, Allelic Discrimination mode).
Identify clusters: samples with both HEX and FAM signals indicate the target is present; samples with HEX only indicate the target is absent; NTCs should show no signal.
Confirm that positive controls cluster with target‑present samples, negative controls with target‑absent samples, and NTCs with the no‑signal cluster.
If clusters are ambiguous, revisit the marker test (extra cycles) or sample preparation.
